steps.prompt: Pick two points on a circle. From every other point on the circle, the angle they make looks about the same. Is it really the same? How does it compare with the angle at the centre?

cards.title: Inscribed angles
cards.body: A central angle equals its arc. An inscribed angle (its corner on the circle) is HALF its arc. So inscribed angles on the same arc are equal, an angle in a semicircle is $90^\circ$, and opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to $180^\circ$.

cards.title: Worked example: half the arc
cards.problem: An inscribed angle of $35^\circ$ cuts off an arc. What is the central angle on that arc? What is another inscribed angle on it?

steps.text: The central angle equals the arc, which is twice the inscribed angle: $70^\circ$.

try.prompt: What is the central angle, in degrees?

steps.text: Every inscribed angle on that arc is half of $70^\circ$: $35^\circ$.

try.prompt: What is another inscribed angle on the same arc?

cards.title: Chords and the centre
cards.body: The perpendicular from the centre to a chord cuts the chord in half. So the radius $r$, the distance $d$ from the centre and half the chord $\frac{c}{2}$ make a right triangle: $r^2 = d^2 + \left(\frac{c}{2}\right)^2$. Draw the radii: they are your best friends.

cards.title: Worked example: chord distance
cards.problem: A circle has radius $13$ and a chord of length $24$. How far is the chord from the centre?

steps.text: The perpendicular from the centre halves the chord.

try.prompt: How long is half the chord?
How far is the chord from the centre?

cards.title: The common trap: equal instead of half
cards.body: An inscribed angle is half the central angle on the same arc, not equal to it. Check where the corner is: at the centre (equal to the arc) or on the circle (half). And opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to $180^\circ$; they aren't equal.

prompts: Why is an angle in a semicircle always a right angle?
